# vibeward — full reference for LLMs

> Security scanner for AI-generated / vibe-coded apps. Finds exposed secrets, missing
> Row-Level Security, insecure backends and local-database exposure — from a URL or from
> your code — and writes a context-rich report that an AI coding tool can turn into a fix.
> Read-only. Open source (MIT). Run with `npx vibeward@latest`. Site: https://vibeward.ai

## Why it exists

Apps built with AI coding tools (Lovable, Bolt, v0, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex) ship fast and
ship the same handful of critical holes. This is documented, not hypothetical:

- CVE-2025-48757 (CVSS 9.3): insufficient Supabase Row-Level Security in Lovable let
  unauthenticated attackers read/write arbitrary tables. 170 of 1,645 analyzed projects
  (10.3%) were vulnerable.
- Moltbook (2026): a vibe-coded app with no RLS policies and a public key in the client bundle
  exposed ~1.5M auth tokens and 35,000 emails.
- Veracode (2026): AI-generated code introduced a known security flaw in 45% of tests, a rate
  ~2.7x higher than human-written code.

## What it scans

Secrets (URL bundles and source code, reported with file:line):
- Supabase service_role key in the client (decoded from the JWT role, so the public anon key
  is not falsely flagged)
- Stripe, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, AWS, GitHub, Resend, SendGrid, Twilio keys
- Private PEM keys and suspicious secret assignments
- Committed .env files

Supabase / Postgres:
- Tables readable without authentication (probed with the public anon key, read-only)
- Migrations: tables created without RLS, permissive `USING (true)` policies, SECURITY DEFINER
  functions
- Optional deep audit via a read-only SQL query you run in the Supabase SQL Editor (no
  credentials shared with the tool)

Backend:
- SQL injection (interpolated queries, Prisma $queryRawUnsafe, Drizzle sql.raw, better-sqlite3)
- Open CORS, command injection, eval / new Function, verbose error leaks

Local database:
- Committed SQLite / .db files (they contain data), including files served from a public folder

HTTP security headers:
- Missing Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options,
  X-Content-Type-Options; technology-stack leaks

## Guardrail (the differentiator)

Most vibe-coded holes start with a prompt. vibeward runs as a Claude Code `UserPromptSubmit` hook
and catches the risky request the moment the user types it — before the agent acts:
- "disable RLS so it works" → blocked, with why + the safe policy to write instead
- "use the service_role key in the frontend" → blocked
- "make the table public to debug" / "remove the login for now" → blocked

The rules are deterministic (regex, no LLM call), so they cannot be prompt-injected away. Install:
```json
{ "hooks": { "UserPromptSubmit": [ { "hooks": [{ "type": "command", "command": "npx vibeward@latest guard" }] } ] } }
```
Use `guard --warn` to warn without blocking.

## Modes (the scanner — a backstop to the guardrail)

Black-box (from a URL) — quick outside-in check:
```
npx vibeward@latest https://your-app.lovable.app
```

White-box (from the code) — deep audit with exact file:line, reads a git repo, a downloaded ZIP,
or a synced folder:
```
npx vibeward@latest scan ./your-app
```

Supabase deep audit without giving credentials:
```
npx vibeward@latest supabase-sql          # run this query in the Supabase SQL Editor
npx vibeward@latest scan ./your-app --supabase result.json
```

CI (GitHub Action) — runs on every push, uploads SARIF to the GitHub Security tab, fails the
build on a critical finding:
```yaml
- uses: JSiapoDEV/vibeward@v1
  with:
    path: '.'
```

## Output

Every finding is a context block designed to be both human-readable and consumable by an AI
coding assistant to open a correct pull request. Each finding includes:
- Classification (CWE)
- Where (URL, bundle, or file:line)
- Evidence (counts, snippets, column names)
- How it's exploited (a concrete abuse path for that instance)
- Impact (quantified: rows, data, money at risk)
- Why it matters (in business language)
- References (CVE, CWE, vendor docs)

Reports are written as Markdown; JSON and SARIF 2.1.0 are also available. Exit code is 2 when a
critical finding is present, for CI gating.

## Authorization

vibeward is strictly read-only: no writes, no deletes, no data exfiltration. It only reads what a
browser would fetch, and confirms database exposure by reading at most one row (storing only the
count and the names of sensitive columns, never row contents). Run it only against applications
whose owner authorized the audit.
